items.title: Why focusing on cap $ can be misleading.
items.body_excerpt:
Why focusing on cap $ can be misleading.

You are conditioned to compare new salaries to past salaries. But the cap keeps rising distorting those comparisons.

Brandin Podziemski signed a 5yr, $110m extension. That same extension starting in 2019-20 season would be 5yr, $67m.

images.alt: Dumbbell chart titled "Brandin Podziemski Contract Extension Compared to If It Started in the 2019-20 Season." For each year of the five-year deal, a gray dot shows the salary at that year's cap percentage applied to a 2019-24 salary cap, and a blue dot shows the projected 2027-32 salary at the same percentage. Year 1, 10.8% of cap: $11.8M at the 2019-20 cap versus $18.9M in 2027-28. Year 2, 11.1%: $12.1M at the 2020-21 cap versus $20.5M in 2028-29. Year 3, 11.3%: $12.7M at the 2021-22 cap versus $22.0M in 2029-30. Year 4, 11.5%: $14.2M at the 2022-23 cap versus $23.5M in 2030-31. Year 5, 11.7%: $15.9M at the 2023-24 cap versus $25.0M in 2031-32. Data: Keith Smith, Spotrac. Viz: @Hoopinformatics.com on Bluesky.
